budget_items.what_was_said: The committee reported total municipal energy consumption fell versus the baseline, meeting the green-communities reduction goal, with the largest drop in buildings.
The annual report narrative stated total municipal, building and vehicle energy use all decreased while water and sewer energy use increased.
The chair reported the November streetlight bill was high but far below what the town paid before it owned its own streetlights.

budget_items.topic: Streetlight savings and a proposed maintenance reserve fund
budget_items.what_was_said: Members said savings from lower streetlight bills have just been absorbed into the general budget with nothing set aside for future LED maintenance, and discussed creating a reserve or special revolving fund instead.
A member said the town badly needs an experienced grant writer, and noted a budgeted grant-writer line had gone unspent before.

budget_items.topic: PPP energy audit and comprehensive building analysis (CBA)
budget_items.what_was_said: National Grid was to provide a free preliminary audit and a comprehensive building analysis of all twelve town buildings, but the committee said it has waited months with no result.

budget_items.topic: Capital outlay override for building projects
budget_items.what_was_said: A member described how the town of Ashby used a one-time capital outlay override to fund and pay off building projects in a single year, and suggested Lunenburg consider it for its aging buildings.
A member said current incentives make an electric riding mower roughly half the price of an equivalent gas model, but the town would need duplicate equipment for separate departments.

budget_items.topic: Capital planning equipment list / mower purchase
budget_items.what_was_said: A member said the school department's capital plan includes buying a new zero-turn mower and the group discussed pushing for an electric model.

A member relayed that capital planning discussed a perceived risk that hybrid police vehicle batteries could be costly once out of warranty, and that gas vehicle quotes may be sought for the next replacement round.

decisions.decision: Committee agreed to consider renaming itself from a Green Community committee toward something like an Energy or Energy and Sustainability Committee.
A member agreed to update the committee's Facebook page with the annual energy report the chair would send.
Chair agreed to push for Tyler's official appointment to an upcoming open committee seat.
Next meeting set for roughly mid-January, once the PPP building audit results are available.

minutes.headline: Committee met its energy-reduction goal but remains stalled awaiting building energy audits needed for Turkey Hill decisions.
minutes.summary: The Green Community Task Force reviewed its FY26 annual energy report, which showed the town hit its energy-reduction goal, with Turkey Hill and the old elementary building flagged as the largest energy users. Most of the meeting covered stalled progress: a National Grid building-energy audit and analysis six months overdue, no reserve fund for future LED streetlight maintenance, an unsuccessful styrofoam-recycling grant push, and broader town indecision on Turkey Hill, Town Hall and other building needs. No substantive votes were taken beyond routine approval of minutes and adjournment; the group discussed renaming itself an energy/sustainability committee and pursuing Tyler's appointment to a soon-open seat.

what_happened.line: The town met its green-communities energy-reduction goal for FY26, with buildings driving most of the drop.
A promised National Grid audit and building-by-building analysis, needed before any Turkey Hill decision, is months overdue with no date given.
Streetlight bill savings are going into the general budget with no reserve set aside for future LED maintenance.
The committee took no votes on policy; it discussed renaming itself an energy/sustainability committee and backing Tyler for an open seat.

why_it_matters: Turkey Hill and Town Hall building decisions, and any capital ask tied to them, are on hold until the overdue energy audit comes back.
Streetlight savings with no maintenance reserve means a future LED repair cost would compete with other budget lines rather than draw on savings already realized.
A committee name change and a pending appointment are procedural and do not commit the town to any spending.
